question.problem: Let $X$ be the number obtained by a fair spinner with five sections labelled $1,2,3,4,5.$ What is $\text{Var}[X]?$
question.worked_solution:
The variance of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{Var}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])^{2}\cdot f(x).
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ Here, there are $5$ possible outcomes ($1,2,3,4,5$) and each outcome has the same probability, so the probability mass function is as follows:

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ |

Now, we need to compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4)+5\cdot f(5) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{5})+2(\frac{1}{5})+3(\frac{1}{5})+4(\frac{1}{5})+5(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[X]=3$ into the variance formula, we get

$$
\text{Var}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}(x-3)^{2}\cdot f(x).
$$

Now, we compute the variance as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =(1-3)^{2}\cdot f(1)+(2-3)^{2}\cdot f(2)+(3-3)^{2}\cdot f(3)+(4-3)^{2}\cdot f(4) \\  & +(5-3)^{2}\cdot f(5) \\  & =4\cdot f(1)+f(2)+0\cdot f(3)+1\cdot f(4)+4\cdot f(5) \\  & =4(\frac{1}{5})+(\frac{1}{5})+0+(\frac{1}{5})+4(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$
